tldr: This thread is a reading list of LLM research grouped by shared wording, not one event. From Anthropic's Nov 2 provable-inference update it ran through agent reliability, serving infrastructure, eval validity and multimodal hallucination to Nov 13-16 papers on when a model should abstain, ask or escalate.
whats_new: Nov 19: a deception study uses label-free knowledge and persona directions to build lie probes that transfer across lie types, and a second paper measures hallucination in cyber-threat-intelligence tasks.
why_it_matters: Most items are single unreplicated preprints, but the recent run converges on detection at serving time (jailbreak screening, calibrated abstention, lie probes), each a component a serving stack can test on its own traffic.

beats.headline: Anthropic reports progress on zkSNARK-based provable inference
beats.summary: The thread's only lab-published item: cryptographic proofs applied to LLM inference.

beats.headline: Agent context, failure analysis and harder agent benchmarks
beats.summary: From context engines and token trimming to where long-horizon errors enter, plus web, multimodal and visual-agent benchmarks.

beats.headline: LLMs and agents aimed at kernels, cache reuse, routing and training simulation
beats.summary: Includes a local 7B code model on GPU kernels, KV-cache reuse across a DeepSeek-V4-Flash update, and what token spend actually measures.

beats.headline: Preference optimization variants: Nash, debate, steerable adapters, token reweighting
Updating what models know: answerability drift, unlearning and knowledge editing
beats.summary: Plus how false corrections and wording change which facts a model can still reach.

beats.headline: What do scores measure? Rater drift, framing, throttling and shortcut probes
beats.summary: Chatbot Arena standards rising, framing effects, models driven to a target score, and recall evals that lean on entity names.

beats.headline: Multimodal hallucination: preference alignment and decoding fixes
beats.summary: Eight papers attack vision and omnimodal models answering beyond their evidence.

beats.headline: Applied one-offs: federated learning, AutoML, diagnostics and anomaly detection
beats.summary: Grouped by shared wording, not by a common thread.

beats.headline: Knowing when not to answer: uncertainty, clarification, triage and calibrated abstention
Detecting bad outputs: jailbreak screening, domain hallucination and lie probes
beats.summary: Nov 18-19 papers target detection at serving time: which prompt to block, where a domain model hallucinates, when a model is lying.

open_questions: Do the Nov 19 knowledge and persona directions detect lies on models outside the study, and at what false-positive rate?
Does the contrastive-prototype jailbreak detector report false-positive rates on benign prompts and hold up against adaptive attacks?
Does stability-compensated threshold calibration keep its error guarantee when the deployed model or prompt distribution shifts?
Does KV-cache reuse across model updates hold beyond the DeepSeek-V4-Flash case study?
Do published unlearning or knowledge-editing methods still pass when probed without explicit entity names, as ShadowBench suggests they may not?
Does Anthropic publish proving cost or latency figures for zkSNARK-based provable inference?
take_for_builders: Before adopting any of these detectors, replay your own traffic: measure the jailbreak screen's false-block rate on benign prompts, check that a calibrated abstention threshold holds its error rate on your data, and count the extra model calls each adds.
